reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It prioritizes building a solid aerobic base with consistent, easy runs, which is crucial for increasing endurance and efficiency – key components of trail speed. Plan B, while including some runs with incline, focuses heavily on ‘easy’ runs and doesn’t incorporate any structured strength work or longer, more challenging sessions that would directly translate to improved speed. Plan A’s inclusion of a dedicated strength and mobility session is a significant advantage for injury prevention and power development, while Plan B’s longer runs, though easy, don’t provide the stimulus needed for significant performance gains.
